+## #2872 - Example case edm/sinker: Sinker Burn and Sinker Side Burn
+
+**Decided.** The case `examples/catalog/edm/sinker` burns one blind
+rectangular cavity (20 x 12 x 8 mm, in a 60 x 40 x 25 mm block) with one
+electrode. A rough Sinker Burn (`R1`) burns the cavity. A Sinker Side Burn
+(`F1`) then burns to the floor and moves the electrode 0.22 mm toward +X
+and back. The +X wall and the floor go to size; the other walls keep the
+rough allowance.
+
+- The machine is the shipped template `Sinker EDM 3-axis (template)`.
+  The build script adds two conditions and all of the sinker code words
+  with `edit_machine`. The values and the words are invented. The README
+  and the script say so.
+- The electrode comes from `electrode_from_faces` over the cavity faces,
+  so the case also shows how an electrode is made. Its `burn` reply seeds
+  both operations.
+- The post is chosen with `add_setup` and `set_setup_post`, as the
+  turning cases do. The regenerate check posts with the document's post.
+- The side amount (0.22 mm) equals the allowance (0.25 undersize - 0.03
+  finish gap). The wall thus reaches its drawn size.
+
+**Why.** The shipped template states no codes, and the post refuses a
+program without them (by design, #3001). An example cannot ship real
+vendor codes (Clean-Room Protocol). Invented, labelled codes show the
+whole flow and keep the program readable.
+
+**Dropped.**
+- A side burn on all four walls: four operations make the program longer
+  and show nothing new about the kind.
+- A new machine file with the codes: a second sinker machine in
+  `assets/machines` would look like a real machine. The patch stays inside
+  the example.
+- A stated electrode with `add_tool`: `electrode_from_faces` is the
+  documented route, and it keeps the electrode size tied to the condition.
+
+**Cost to change.** Low. Edit `build.camscript` and run
+`cargo xtask catalog --case edm/sinker`. The pin
+`sinker_case_posts_the_burn_and_the_side_burn` states the depths and the
+lateral X values, so it changes with them.

+# Sinker (Sinker Burn, Sinker Side Burn)
+
+A 60 x 40 x 25 mm clean-room block with one blind rectangular cavity.
+The cavity is 20 x 12 mm and 8 mm deep (floor `Z17`), centred at `(5, 0)`.
+A sinker EDM burns it with one rectangular electrode.
+
+The machine is the shipped template `Sinker EDM 3-axis (template)`.
+The template states no conditions and no codes.
+The build script adds them with `edit_machine`.
+The two conditions and all of the code words are invented for this example.
+They are not the codes of any control.
+Before you use a real machine, take its conditions and codes from the control's manual.
+
+| Condition | Role | Spark gap per side | Undersize per side |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `R1` | rough | 0.10 mm | 0.25 mm |
+| `F1` | finish | 0.03 mm | 0.03 mm |
+
+## What it shows
+
+1. **Electrode (`E-19.5x11.5`):** `electrode_from_faces` makes the electrode from the cavity's floor and four walls.
+   The `R1` undersize makes it 0.25 mm smaller per side: 19.5 x 11.5 mm.
+2. **Sinker Burn (`Rough burn`, condition `R1`, pass `rough`):** The electrode sinks at `(5, 0)` in one servo block, `M101 Z17.25 F50.`.
+   A rough pass leaves 0.15 mm (0.25 undersize - 0.10 gap) on each wall and on the floor.
+   Thus the electrode tip stops at the floor + 0.15 + 0.10 = `Z17.25`.
+3. **Sinker Side Burn (`Side burn +X`, condition `F1`):** The electrode sinks again to the floor + the finish gap, `Z17.03`.
+   This takes the floor to its drawn depth.
+   Then the electrode moves 0.22 mm toward +X and back, at that depth: two `M102` blocks.
+   The move puts the +X wall at its drawn size (0.25 undersize - 0.03 finish gap = 0.22).
+   The other three walls keep the 0.15 mm rough allowance.
+
+## What to look at
+
+- In `sinker.nc`, find the two `(OPERATION: ...)` sections.
+  Each section selects its condition (`ER1`, `EF1`) before its burn.
+- Only the side burn section has `M102` blocks.
+  The first goes to `X5.22`, and the second comes back to `X5.`.
+  `Y` and `Z` do not change during the lateral move.
+- A straight burn moves the electrode in Z only.
+  A side burn moves one wall out by a stated amount.
+  CamCraft refuses an amount larger than the undersize minus the condition's gap.
+- The post refuses a Side Burn if the machine does not state the `side` code.
+
+## Files
+
+- `model/gen_sinker_obj.py` — watertight voxel-CSG generator for the block and its cavity.
+- `model/sinker.obj` — generated quad mesh imported by `build.camscript`.
+- `build.camscript` — headless script that builds `sinker.camproj` and posts `sinker.nc` through CamCraft's undoable commands.
+- `case.toml` — operation kinds, machine and expected result.
+- `sinker.camproj` — committed project with generated toolpaths.
+- `sinker.nc` — committed program, checked byte for byte in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`.
+
+## Rebuild and verify
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+cargo xtask catalog --case edm/sinker
+cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog
+```

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Regenerate sinker.obj, the model of the catalog case edm/sinker (#2872).
+
+The part is a clean-room Camcraft fixture: a 60 x 40 x 25 mm block of
+hardened die steel with one blind rectangular cavity, 20 x 12 mm and 8 mm
+deep (floor at z = 17), centred at (5, 0). A sinker EDM burns the cavity
+with a rectangular electrode, so its walls are sharp and vertical: the
+shape a milling cutter cannot leave in the corners.
+
+Method: the solid is the block minus the cavity box. Both boxes have faces
+on one plane set, so the boundary is built exactly by voxel CSG over that
+grid: every inside/outside cell face is emitted as a unit quad. Unit quads
+tile every plane the same way from both sides, so the mesh is conforming
+(no T-junctions), watertight, and consistently outward-oriented; the
+script self-checks that before writing.
+
+Usage: python gen_sinker_obj.py [output.obj]
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+BLOCK = (-30.0, 30.0, -20.0, 20.0, 0.0, 25.0)   # x0 x1 y0 y1 z0 z1
+CAVITY = (-5.0, 15.0, -6.0, 6.0, 17.0, 25.0)
+
+XS = [-30.0, -5.0, 15.0, 30.0]
+YS = [-20.0, -6.0, 6.0, 20.0]
+ZS = [0.0, 17.0, 25.0]
+PLANES = [XS, YS, ZS]
+
+
+def inside_box(p, box):
+    x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1 = box
+    return x0 <= p[0] <= x1 and y0 <= p[1] <= y1 and z0 <= p[2] <= z1
+
+
+def solid(p):
+    return inside_box(p, BLOCK) and not inside_box(p, CAVITY)
+
+
+def build():
+    dims = [len(p) - 1 for p in PLANES]
+    inside = set()
+    for i in range(dims[0]):
+        for j in range(dims[1]):
+            for k in range(dims[2]):
+                mid = [(PLANES[a][idx] + PLANES[a][idx + 1]) / 2
+                       for a, idx in enumerate((i, j, k))]
+                if solid(tuple(mid)):
+                    inside.add((i, j, k))
+
+    groups = {}
+    for cell in inside:
+        for axis in range(3):
+            for sign in (+1, -1):
+                nxt = list(cell)
+                nxt[axis] += sign
+                if tuple(nxt) in inside:
+                    continue
+                plane = cell[axis] + (1 if sign > 0 else 0)
+                a, b = (d for d in range(3) if d != axis)
+                groups.setdefault((axis, plane, sign, a, b), set()).add(
+                    (cell[a], cell[b]))
+
+    # with a, b the other two axes in ascending order, walking (a then b)
+    # gives a normal of +axis for axis 0 and 2 and -axis for axis 1
+    # (hat{x} x hat{z} = -hat{y}), so check that sign before emitting
+    WALK_SIGN = {0: +1, 1: -1, 2: +1}
+    quads = []  # each a list of 4 (x, y, z) coordinate tuples, oriented
+    for (axis, plane, sign, a, b), cells in sorted(groups.items()):
+        for (ca, cb) in sorted(cells):
+            quad = []
+            for p, q in [(ca, cb), (ca + 1, cb), (ca + 1, cb + 1), (ca, cb + 1)]:
+                pos = [None, None, None]
+                pos[axis] = PLANES[axis][plane]
+                pos[a] = PLANES[a][p]
+                pos[b] = PLANES[b][q]
+                quad.append(tuple(pos))
+            if WALK_SIGN[axis] != sign:
+                quad.reverse()
+            quads.append(quad)
+    return quads
+
+
+def check(quads):
+    """Watertight and consistently oriented: every directed edge appears
+    exactly once and its reverse appears exactly once."""
+    seen = {}
+    for quad in quads:
+        for p, q in zip(quad, quad[1:] + quad[:1]):
+            if p == q:
+                raise SystemExit("degenerate quad: %r" % (quad,))
+            if (p, q) in seen:
+                raise SystemExit("directed edge reused: %r -> %r" % (p, q))
+            seen[(p, q)] = True
+    for (p, q) in seen:
+        if (q, p) not in seen:
+            raise SystemExit("open edge: %r -> %r" % (p, q))
+
+
+def main():
+    out = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "sinker.obj"
+    quads = build()
+    check(quads)
+
+    vid = {}
+    vlines = []
+    for quad in quads:
+        for p in quad:
+            if p not in vid:
+                vid[p] = len(vlines) + 1
+                vlines.append("v %g %g %g" % p)
+    flines = []
+    for quad in quads:
+        flines.append("f " + " ".join(str(vid[p]) for p in quad))
+
+    with open(out, "w", newline="\n") as fh:
+        fh.write(HEADER)
+        fh.write("\n" + "\n".join(vlines) + "\n\n" + "\n".join(flines) + "\n")
+    print("wrote %s: %d vertices, %d faces" % (out, len(vlines), len(flines)))
+
+
+HEADER = """\
+# Camcraft catalog case edm/sinker: a 60 x 40 x 25 mm block with one blind
+# rectangular cavity, 20 x 12 mm and 8 mm deep (floor z = 17), centred at
+# (5, 0), for a sinker EDM burn. Authored for this repository (clean-room
+# fixture); generated by gen_sinker_obj.py, this watertight quad mesh is
+# what the example project embeds as facets."""
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
